tax.name: Arkansas state and local sales tax plus the 2% tourism tax

note_add: No park entrance fee (Crater of Diamonds charges separately for its diamond search area, which is not camping). Campsites carry state and local sales tax plus the 2% tourism tax, at a rate that varies by park; the old self-pay sites were posted tax-included. Eight people per site at most, day visitors not counted; one car may park at the site and further vehicles go to designated parking, with no charge stated. No non-resident camping rate appears in the last published fee schedule (2021), but rates are now set by date and demand, so that is not recorded as a zero.

note_add: Rates do not include state and local taxes. A site takes one camping unit, defined as the camper plus one more vehicle; more vehicles or boat trailers park where the site manager allows. Six people per site at most. The camping fee schedule (LAC 25:IX 504) has no residency split, though it lets the agency surcharge for demand, special events or use beyond a site's capacity. Every state park also charges a per-person general admission (LAC 25:IX 500, about $3 a person, seniors and small children free), and the rules do not exempt registered campers or say whether it is charged once a stay or daily.

note_add: Mississippi sales tax is added where applicable. The fee schedule (40 Miss. Admin. Code Part 6, Rule 1.1) prices RV sites by the night with no per-person, per-vehicle or non-resident charge; the annual entrance pass is the same in and out of state. Eight people per site at most, visitors included; one extra tent may go on a site with the manager's approval at the primitive rate. Entrance is $0-4 a person by park (5 and under free); an RV site's rental covers fishing and the boat launch for those registered on it, visitors pay entrance, and the rules leave unclear whether registered campers do.

tax.name: Alabama state lodgings tax plus local lodging taxes

note_add: Campsites carry Alabama's lodgings tax plus local lodging taxes, at a rate that varies by park (4% at Paul Grist, 17% at Oak Mountain); some parks add a resort fee (3.75% at Oak Mountain). Per-person park admission is set park by park ($3-5 an adult) and whether registered campers pay it is not stated; at some parks visitors of campers pay per vehicle. Occupancy limits (eight people, two vehicles at Oak Mountain) are posted park by park.

tax.name: Florida 6% sales tax plus county taxes

note_add: The camping fee includes park admission for the registered campers and the use of boat ramps and playgrounds, not tours or museums. Every new booking of an RV site with electric and water pays a $7 nightly utility fee, which the 50% Florida senior and disability discount does not cover (nor the $6.70 reservation fee); primitive tent sites skip both. Rates are posted plus tax: Florida's 6% transient-rental tax on RV-park space plus county taxes, which vary by county. Cancelling costs $17.75 and changing a booking $10.
